historical_reviews.deepseek: The mutation/readback is only a fragment and its Last-State result contradicts AlwaysOff; it omits BMC-reset persistence, both AC scenarios, CPU service, recovery and protected secrets.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly phases the persistent policy write, controller reset, AC behavior and ESD-controlled CPU replacement with independent restoration.
historical_reviews.history: No earlier exact source identity record exists.
historical_reviews.v3_1: AlwaysOff must keep the host off after AC returns regardless of whether the pre-loss host state was on or off. The later CPU-swap checkpoint has a different oracle—successful deliberate power-on and no reboot loop—so its evidence must not be conflated with automatic restore behavior.

original_test_intent: Prove AlwaysOff policy persistence across a BMC cold reset and AC loss from both host states, then separately verify successful controlled boot after the specified compatible CPU swap.
original_method: Capture and restore the policy/hardware baseline; set AlwaysOff through a supported protected interface and verify it before/after BMC reset; run separately approved physical AC scenarios from on and off and confirm the host remains off; then under ESD-safe service controls swap the approved CPU pair and deliberately power on to verify POST, boot and health.
manual_activity: An operator authorizes and performs the BMC reset/AC phases, then separately performs the powered-down ESD-safe CPU service, observes POST/boot and owns recovery and verdict.
required_inputs: Maintenance window, workload backup and independent recovery
Exact old/new CPU part and serial matrix
BIOS, microcode, power and thermal compatibility
ESD-safe service and socket recovery procedure
safety_requirements: Separate approvals for policy, reset, AC and CPU phases
Verify exact PDU outlet and CPU target
Use protected secrets and supported commands
Never service CPU with any power present
Stop on policy mismatch, unexpected power-on, reboot loop, alarm or POST failure
Restore original policy/hardware and never auto-retry
agent_execution_scope: Verify target and supported policy mapping
Capture baseline and protected set/readback evidence
Monitor BMC reset persistence and AC timelines
Collect POST, inventory, boot and health evidence

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The chassis-policy command is relevant only if vendor-supported, but exposed credentials, no protected mapping and the incorrect Last-State narration make the fragment unsafe and incomplete.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use protected supported AlwaysOff set/readback with captured baseline; gate BMC reset, each AC action and CPU replacement behind separate operator approvals and evidence checkpoints.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The 10/20-minute estimates, BMC reset, both AC states and CPU swap remain; no automatic physical action or log clearing is introduced.

modernized_recommendation.status: PHASED ALWAYSOFF PERSISTENCE AND CPU-SERVICE VALIDATION
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Maintain separate evidence ledgers for policy persistence, two AlwaysOff AC trials and the CPU replacement/intentional-boot trial, joined only by exact target and baseline restoration.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds supported mapping, per-phase approvals, ESD/compatibility controls and independent recovery.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A successful set/readback does not prove reset persistence, AC behavior or post-replacement boot stability.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A BMC reset can interrupt management while CPU replacement can create socket, firmware and thermal faults; stable power and independent console recovery are mandatory.

project_override_considerations: The Project must define the supported policy interface, CPU pair and issue-specific acceptance. The CPU phase is retained as a distinct checkpoint and must not be used to reinterpret AlwaysOff as LastState.
expected_evidence: Approved exact target, baseline policy/hardware, backup and recovery
Protected AlwaysOff set/readback before and after BMC reset
On-pre-loss and off-pre-loss AC timelines both ending with host off
CPU part/serial, compatibility and ESD service record
Deliberate post-swap POST/boot/topology/thermal/health and no-reboot-loop evidence
Restored original policy/CPU/workload, preserved logs and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently define AlwaysOff plus an explicit CPU-swap boot checkpoint. DeepSeek's Last-State wording is an erroneous review interpretation, not a competing Master requirement.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Policy mapping, controlled PDU access, compatible CPU/BIOS matrix, ESD service, backup and recovery are normal prerequisites; absence after request or inability to restore safely would block execution, not this review.

review_improvement: Corrects the Last-State misinterpretation and turns a mixed high-risk procedure into separately approved, recoverable policy, AC and CPU phases.
independent_technical_reasoning: AlwaysOff acceptance is independent of the pre-loss host state: auxiliary power restoration must not cause host power-on. A later deliberate boot after CPU replacement tests compatibility and reboot stability, not AC-restore policy. Keeping these state machines separate prevents a successful manual boot from masking an automatic-power defect.
